stem: Silicon is the second most abundant element by mass in the Earth's crust.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
In industry, silicon is extracted from $\text{SiO}_2$ by reaction with carbon at over $2000^{\circ}\text{C}$.

reaction 1 $$\text{SiO}_2\text{(s)} + 2\text{C(s)} \rightarrow \text{Si(l)} + 2\text{CO(g)}$$
parts.text: Explain why the entropy change, $\Delta S$, of reaction 1 is positive.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Reaction 1 is highly endothermic.

Suggest the effect of an increase in temperature on the feasibility of this reaction.
Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Silicon is purified by first heating it in a stream of $\text{HCl(g)}$ to form $\text{SiHCl}_3$. The $\text{SiHCl}_3$ formed is then distilled to remove other impurities.

reaction 2 $$\text{Si(s)} + 3\text{HCl(g)} \rightarrow \text{SiHCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$
parts.text:
Table 2.1 shows some standard entropy data.

Table 2.1

| compound | standard entropy, $\text{S}^{\ominus}/\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{Si(s)}$ | 19 |
| $\text{HCl(g)}$ | 187 |
| $\text{SiHCl}_3\text{(g)}$ | 314 |
| $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ | 131 |

Use the data in Table 2.1 to calculate $\Delta S^{\ominus}$ for reaction 2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Reaction 3 is the reverse of reaction 2 and is used to obtain pure silicon.

reaction 3 $$\text{SiHCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{Si(s)} + 3\text{HCl(g)} \quad \Delta H = +219.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

Use this information and your answer to (b)(i) to calculate the temperature, in K, at which reaction 3 becomes feasible.
Show your working.

[If you were unable to answer (b)(i), you should use $\Delta S^{\ominus} = -150\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ for reaction 2. This is not the correct answer to (b)(i).]

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Silicon can also be produced by electrolysis of $\text{SiO}_2$ dissolved in molten $\text{CaCl}_2$. The relevant half-equation for the cathode is shown.

$$\text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Si} + 2\text{O}^{2-}$$

Calculate the time, in seconds, required to produce $1.00\text{ g}$ of $\text{Si}$ by this electrolysis, using a current of $6.00\text{ A}$.
Assume no other substances are produced at the cathode.
